Weekend

Create, develop, and pitch a business idea in just 50+ hours for a chance to win $10,000!

Get ready for RampUp Weekend 2026! Held April 10–12, 2026, North Forge’s flagship 50+ hour competition will once again bring together aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, and tech enthusiasts to transform bold startup ideas into viable business plans. Past winners have gone on to build multi-million dollar companies — proof that Manitoba is home to the talent and entrepreneurial spirit needed to create globally competitive businesses and fuel local economic growth.

RAMPUP Weekend 2026
Fri, Apr 10
100 Innovation Dr
Details

April 10-12, 2026

North Forge’s RampUp Weekend is an intense, hands-on event where aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, and tech enthusiasts come together to develop startup ideas from concept to viable business plans within a short time frame, typically 50 hours.

 

Participants pitch their ideas, form teams, and work collaboratively to build a minimum viable product (MVP). With mentorship from industry experts and access to resources like the North Forge FabLab, teams refine their business models and prototypes. The event culminates in a final pitch competition, where teams present their projects to a panel of judges, often leading to prizes, investment opportunities, or further support from North Forge’s programs.

 

This event is designed to accelerate the startup process, foster collaboration, and provide participants with a real-world experience of what it takes to launch a successful business.

New for 2026:

To keep the kickoff event fast-paced, memorable, and fair for everyone, we’ve updated the pitch process this year. Here's how it works:

​

Step 1: Submit a 1-minute video pitch
Anyone who wants to pitch their startup idea must submit a one-minute video explaining their idea. Judges will not watch past one minute. 

​

Step 2: Purchase a Pitch Ticket
When submitting your video, you’ll also purchase a Pitch Ticket ($10) for RampUp Weekend. This small fee helps North Forge continue to deliver a high-quality event and provide meaningful support to founders in our ecosystem.
 

Step 3: Top 30 Ideas Pitch Live

A North Forge judging panel will review all submissions and select the 30 most promising ideas to pitch live at the RampUp Weekend Friday kickoff event.
 

But here’s the twist…You won’t know if your idea was selected until the live event on Friday night. All founders who submitted a pitch will sit in the audience. Throughout the evening, the 30 selected founders will be called to the podium at random to deliver their one-minute pitch.
 

Step 4: Audience Voting

After the 30 pitches are complete, the audience will vote for their top three favourite ideas. The 10 ideas with the most votes will move forward into the weekend to build teams and develop their startup.

PURCHASE A TICKET & SUBMIT YOUR PITCH HERE.
Submissions due by 5 p.m. on Sunday, April 5.

​

How it Works

🚀 Friday - APRIL 10

The energy kicks off with rapid-fire pitches — just 60 seconds to sell an idea! This year, 30 founders are selected from video submissions, but they won’t know if they’re pitching until they’re called up live during the event. Once all pitches are delivered, the crowd votes and the top 10 ideas move forward. Those founders handpick their dream teams, and the real work begins — brainstorming, strategizing, and mapping out the business’s game plan.

🔥 Saturday - APRIL 11

It's full-speed ahead! Logos are designed, websites launched, prototypes built, and real customer validation happens in real-time...it’s an entrepreneurial tornado! Expert mentors roam the rooms, pushing teams to refine their ideas and navigate the inevitable pivots.

🎤 Sunday - APRIL 12

The stakes are high, and the pressure is on! Teams fine-tune their business models, polish their pitches, and get last-minute coaching from mentors. Then teams take the stage for the final showdown! Five minutes to pitch, five minutes for judges’ Q&A, and then...it’s decision time. Prizes, recognition, and maybe even the launch of Manitoba’s next game-changing startup! Come cheer on the teams at the Pinnacle Club at Princess Auto Stadium!

Notable Companies from RampUP include

Permission click is software that creates digital permission slips and facilitates payment collection for kindergarten to grade 12, was recently acquired by Intrado Corporation for its innovative product.

Taiv is a TV box that allows restaurants and bars to play content that is better targeted to their audiences.

Go Oil is a mobile oil change company, has sold over 40+ franchises in Canada and the United States!

    • Your solution

Meet the Judges

Iain Crozier

Founder and Managing Partner, Trillick Ventures

Iain Crozier is a dedicated father of four, seasoned entrepreneur and venture capitalist. At Trillick Ventures he brings deep operator-led experience to venture investing. He previously led and scaled a 25-year-old family business by 7x in seven years, leading to a successful exit.  Today, he leverages his background to mentor founders, advise leadership teams and help build a stronger, more investable startup ecosystem in Manitoba.

Katie Hall Hursh

VP, Megill-Stephensen Company & Managing Partner, Women's Equity Lab

Katie Hall Hursh provides strategic leadership to Megill’s subsidiaries while championing the development of greater access to capital for early-stage companies through WEL. Passionate about building sustainable enterprises and advancing economic equity, Katie is committed to strengthening both the business community and the innovation ecosystem in Manitoba.

Dennis Agbeha

 Director, the Prairies at RBCx 

Dennis Agbegha currently leads the RBCx regional team across Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba, supporting RBCx clients while building strategic client relationships to drive growth. He stewards RBCx in the market, fostering strong relationships within the ecosystem, and provides insights and guidance to startups, companies and internal banking partners.

Become a RampUp mentor

As a RampUp Weekend Mentor, you will be able to provide guidance, advice, and guide our aspiring entrepreneurs through the tough problems and pain points they’re trying to solve. An experienced mentor like you will impart knowledge, expertise, and wisdom from your area of expertise to enhance their mentees’ business ideas.

Mentors for roles and fields include but are not limited to:

  • Marketing and branding

  • Graphic Design, User Experience and User Interface (UX, UI)

  • Sales

  • Accounting

  • Business Advising

  • Business Model Development

  • Advanced Manufacturing

  • Engineering

  • Back End Developer

  • Front End Developer

  • Pitch Scrubbing

  • Youth Mentorship

What do you gain as a RampUp mentor?

 

You’re able to connect and learn from the diverse perspectives of our participants from various backgrounds and generations.

Individuals of all ages and with different backgrounds think and act in different ways – we want all perspectives! Our participants range from post-secondary students, professional students, and workers, to retired individuals! The business relationship between a mentor and a mentee allows for people to learn similar ways of thinking and differences that could provide innovative perspectives and solutions.

 

Gain the opportunity to make a change in someone’s entrepreneurial journey!

You’ll be first in our participants’ minds! Do you remember the teacher, boss, or coach who did or said something that impacted your life in a positive way? Step into the opportunity to do that for someone else!

​

Able to strengthen your knowledge, experiences, and lessons.
Put your knowledge and lessons into practice by sharing them with the community! Guide our participants through challenges, point out common problems, and enrich the lessons you learned with fresh perspectives.

Land acknowledgement

North Forge is located on Treaty One Territory and in the National Homeland of the Red River Métis. We honour the Anishinaabeg, Anisininew (Oji-Cree), Ininiwak (Cree), Oceti Sakowin/Dakota Oyate, and Michif (Métis) Peoples as the original caretakers of this land. With gratitude and reciprocity, we recognize the songs, stories, teachings, and knowledge systems rooted here. The Treaties were entered into in good faith, as agreements to share, not surrender, the land. We are committed to upholding the spirit and intent of these agreements, and to building a future grounded in truth, equity, and meaningful collaboration. Read our full land acknowledgement and commitments.
